newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO GAS OIL EXPORTS SEEN ACTIVE, NAPHTHA HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO GAS OIL EXPORTS SEEN ACTIVE, NAPHTHA HIGHER.

text.p: The Tokyo oil products market remained in the summer doldrums on Tuesday except for gas oil, with several oil firms said to be offering gas oil cargoes aggressively amid ample domestic availability, market participants said.
A spot gas oil cargo was recently sold at about the mean of Singapore quotes minus $1.25 per barrel FOB (free on board) Mizushima, western Japan, product traders said.
Most gas oil cargoes out of Japan are believed to be destined for China, they added.

Bids for open-spec naphtha, Asia's benchmark forward contract, were heard at $206.00 per tonne for second-half October delivery, while offers were quoted 50 cents higher. It traded between Japanese traders at $205.00 on Monday.
Naphtha levels rebounded for the first time in four business days, trailing modest crude gains on overseas markets.
